config_text:
# Lane B on EMPIAR-11538 again, at MDC Berlin (max cluster), from files already
# on disk: five more untreated series, nothing to download.
#
# Every value below [data] is ribo-bin8.toml's, unchanged: same dataset, same
# detector, same pixel size, so the reasons given there hold here. Only the
# project, the series, the data paths and the Slurm lines are this site's.

[lane]
name = "ribo-bin8"
input = "stack"           # one assembled stack per series, no movies
variant = "bin8"          # label applied from the stack rebuild onward

[run]
project = "outputs/ribo-mdc"
series = ["TS_0306", "TS_0463", "TS_0493", "TS_0564", "TS_0623"]

# Partitions from `sinfo -s` on max (2026-10-14): `normal` is the default, `gpu`
# the GPU nodes, both with a 7-day limit; no QoS is asked for.
#
# The GPU type is pinned to the A40 (45 GB, compute 8.6), the most common card
# there (`sinfo -p gpu -o "%N %G"`). An unpinned request could land on a T4
# (15 GB) or a 16 GB V100, while the bin8 ribosome pick has only been run in a
# 20 GB MIG slice in Munich. CUDA 13, which the env's torch is built for, also
# dropped Volta (compute 7.0); not tried on these nodes.
[[run.stage]]
name = "cpu"
from = "generate-fiducial-seed"
until = "reconstruct-tomogram"
time = "10:00:00"
sbatch = ["--partition=normal", "--cpus-per-task=8", "--mem=32G"]

[[run.stage]]
name = "gpu"
from = "prepare-template"
until = "extract-particles"
time = "16:00:00"
sbatch = ["--partition=gpu", "--gres=gpu:a40:1", "--cpus-per-task=8", "--mem=64G"]

[data]
# Absolute: the data sit beside the clone, not inside it. {series} is per series.
mdoc = "/fast/AG_Kudryashev/{{USER}}/EMPIAR-11538/mdoc/{series}.mrc.mdoc"
stack = "/fast/AG_Kudryashev/{{USER}}/EMPIAR-11538/{series}.mrc"

[binning]
# CTF is fitted on a finer stack and transferred, because a fit at coarse
# binning is badly constrained and does not say so.
#
# The fit stack is built WITHOUT a variant label on purpose: the lane rule is
# that a lookup prefers a labelled candidate and otherwise falls back to the
# shared unlabelled one, never to another lane's. A labelled CTF model would
# therefore be invisible to `correct-ctf --variant bin8`.
# Pick the fit binning by its Nyquist limit, not by the binning number. The fit
# window closes at the stack's Nyquist, and a real fit reaches 6-8 A, so the fit
# stack's Nyquist has to be finer than that or the stack caps the fit:
#
#   bin1  1.223 A/px   Nyquist  2.4 A   spare resolution, 4 GB stack
#   bin2  2.446 A/px   Nyquist  4.9 A   finer than 6-8 A          <- use this
#   bin4  4.892 A/px   Nyquist  9.8 A   coarser than 6-8 A, caps the fit
#   bin8  9.784 A/px   Nyquist 19.6 A
#
# Lane A in the runbook fitted at 2.7 A/px and saw a bin8 fit at 5.4 A/px diverge
# on a high-tilt view. bin4 here is 4.9 A/px, which is that same bad regime, so
# matching lane A means bin2 rather than bin4 on this data.
ctf_fit = 2               # 2.45 A/px, Nyquist 4.9 A, stack 2048^2
tomogram = 8              # 9.78 A/px, Nyquist 19.6 A, 512^2, ribosome ~31 px

[align]
binning = 8               # coarse alignment works on a reduced stack
# Raised from ribo-bin8's 0.2, which excluded nothing on TS_0306. There the
# per-view std over the median falls smoothly from 1.13 near +9 deg (the
# lamella's pretilt, judging by where the curve peaks and by the -52..+68 range
# being centred there) to ~0.7 at both ends; thicker ice gives less contrast.
# Patch tracking failed at the ends: fine alignment found 5.7-11.8 nm residuals
# on -52..-42 and +62..+68 against ~2 nm in the middle, the views look black in
# 3dmod, and 227/1525 points over 5 px exceeded max_pruned_fraction.
#
# 0.84 drops -52..-42 (0.69-0.84) and +60..+68 (0.70-0.82), 11 of 61 views, all
# about 50 deg or more from the lamella normal; -40 (0.864, 3.2 nm) and +58
# (0.842) stay. It was FITTED to TS_0306's residuals, on a curve with no gap in
# it, so it is not yet a rule: check per series that the cut falls where the
# fine-alignment residuals rise, since a thicker or thinner lamella puts the
# same ratio at another angle.
min_std_ratio = 0.84
# Deliberately not set, but NOT because coarse alignment searches for it — it does
# not. With no override, _tilt_axis_angle takes rotation_angle_deg from the manifest
# and returns angle - 90, and that value goes to `tiltxcorr -rotation` as an input.
# So the coarse stage reports back the number it was given, and comparing it against
# the mdoc proves nothing.
#
# The measured axis comes from fine alignment, which parses it out of tiltalign's own
# log. Compare that against 83.6, which the MRC label and the mdoc both record.
# tilt_axis_angle = 83.6

[qc_coarse]
preview_binning = 16
residual_warning_px = 2.0

[fiducials]
# Confirmed by eye in 3dmod: TS_0005 has no gold. So patch tracking, which has
# never been run against real IMOD from this pipeline — expect to debug it.
seed_backend = "imod-patch-seed"
track_backend = "imod-patch-track"

# The user-facing knobs are patch COUNT and OVERLAP; the patch size in pixels is
# derived, mirroring etomo's own sizing:
#
#   usable    = binned_width - 2 * margin
#   patch_px  = usable / (1 + (count - 1) * (1 - overlap))
#
# At 4096 px and pre_binning 8 the tracking stack is 512 px, so these values give
#   usable   = 512 - 52 = 460 px
#   patch    = 460 / (1 + 4 * 0.67) = 125 binned px = 1000 raw px = 1223 A = 122 nm
#
# The margin is etomo's: IMOD's makecomfile trims 5% of the binned size from each
# edge, int(0.05 * 512 + 0.5) = 26 px, which leaves the patches 81% of the image's
# area. The 100 px used until 2026-10-27 left them 37%. Foreshortening asks for no
# margin: tiltxcorr places the patches on the view nearest zero tilt, and on the
# other views they move toward the tilt axis by cos(tilt), so they stay in frame.
# The margin keeps patches off the blank edges newstack leaves when it prealigns;
# the coarse shifts of TS_0306 reach 7 binned px. At 26 px all 25 patches were
# tracked through all 61 views of TS_0306, as at 100 (local IMOD run).
#
# Tuning, from the QC readout after track-fiducials:
#   coverage below the 0.8 warning     -> fewer patches (3x3, 4x4): bigger patches,
#                                         stronger signal per patch
#   coverage fine, fine-align residual -> more patches (6x6, 7x7): finer sampling,
#     high                                weaker signal per patch. 7x7 gives 91 px
#                                         here, close to the old 84.
#   patches failing at the edges       -> raise margin. The tilt axis is 83.6 deg
#                                         from the image Y axis (IMOD's convention),
#                                         so nearly horizontal in the raw frames.
# Below 32 px the sizing refuses rather than producing a useless grid.
#
# Trap: a margin set here is in BINNED pixels, so it does not scale with
# pre_binning; raising pre_binning for contrast means scaling it down by the same
# factor (16 / 13 gives a 62 px = 1213 A patch). Left unset, the margin is the
# default, 5% of the binned image per axis: the same 26 here, and it follows
# pre_binning by itself.
pre_binning = 8
num_patches_x = 5
num_patches_y = 5
patch_overlap = 0.33
patch_margin_px = 26      # binned pixels, not raw; 5% of 512, as etomo trims

# The bandpass tiltxcorr correlates through, in cycles/pixel. IMOD's standard
# recommendations, left at their defaults. This is the knob to reach for if the
# correlation itself fails on low-contrast lamella data rather than the geometry
# being wrong — a symptom that looks like poor coverage everywhere at once, not
# at the edges. Values must be above zero.
# patch_filter_sigma1 = 0.03    # high-pass sigma
# patch_filter_radius2 = 0.25   # low-pass cutoff radius
# patch_filter_sigma2 = 0.05    # low-pass falloff sigma

[fine_align]
robust_fitting = true
auto_prune_outliers = true

# Patch points are coplanar, so the two-plane fit that suits gold beads has no
# two surfaces to find. On TS_0002 it sorted 25 points into 11 and 14 and put the
# planes 10 nm apart; the geometry it then recommended (X axis tilt -1.37 deg,
# tilt angle change -9.34) is a fit to that non-existent split, and the one-plane
# fit on the same points said -3.00 and -7.62 instead. Those are the numbers the
# reconstruction is positioned with, so this is not a reporting detail.
#
# It does NOT fix the recommended thickness. "Thickness needed to contain centers
# of all fiducials" was 172 unbinned px = 21 nm under either fit, because
# coplanar points have no depth to measure — a bead pair on two faces does. So
# reconstruction thickness stays an explicit number for every patch-tracked
# series; see [reconstruct].
surfaces_to_analyze = 1

# The 0.02 default was set for bead tracking, where an outlier is a stray point.
# With a 5x5 patch grid over 59 views there are 1475 points and one patch that
# fails everywhere is 59 of them — 4.0% — so a single bad patch already exceeds
# the default and fine alignment refuses rather than pruning. A patch landing on
# a featureless region, a crack, or the lamella edge is expected and local, and
# dropping it is the right answer.
#
# Derive the limit as "up to two whole patches", not a round number:
#
#   max_pruned_fraction = 2 / num_patches = 2 / 25 = 0.08
#
# More than two of twenty-five failing is no longer a couple of bad regions; it
# is wrong geometry or wrong parameters, and the refusal is correct again.
#
# Only raise this after checking that the outliers really are concentrated in one
# or two contours in the initial tiltalign log. Scattered across many patches
# means the alignment is poor and a higher limit would hide it.
#
# Checked on TS_0002 before setting it: 24 of the 30 worst projection points
# belonged to contours 13 and 23, both failing on views 1-13 where the tilt is
# -51 to -28 deg, and the 3-D point table put those two at 3.8 and 5.0 nm against
# 0.6-1.6 nm for the other twenty-three. Two whole patches, which is what this
# limit is sized for. It was not free to leave at 0.02: the run's largest
# residual was 20.95 px, above the 20 px failure threshold, so without pruning
# fine alignment ends in `fail` rather than merely refusing to prune.
#
# Here three patches, not two: 3 / 25 = 0.12. TS_0493 (MDC run, 2026-10-14)
# pruned 123/1350 = 9.1%, all of it in patches 4, 9 and 14 (mean residuals 9.0,
# 8.0 and 4.6 nm against 0.5-2.4 nm for the other 22), with no view-dependent
# failure left after min_std_ratio. The three sit in one column of the grid,
# image X ~313 binned px, and their residuals are almost all along Y. Patches 4
# and 14 are also among the three worst in TS_0463, a different lamella, which
# would happen by chance about 3% of the time: possibly something fixed on the
# camera at ~2504 unbinned px. Not checked; averaging a raw stack would show it.
max_pruned_fraction = 0.12

[ctf]
voltage_kv = 300.0
# 2.7 mm is the Krios objective, and the MRC label plus the EMDB header both say
# FEI Titan Krios. Checked and not found: the mdoc has Voltage but no Cs, and the
# EMD-16721 header has no spherical-aberration field at all. Only the paper's
# methods would state it. Left at 2.7 because at the bin2 fit limit the Cs term is
# under 1% of the CTF phase, so even a large error in it is not measurable here.
spherical_aberration_mm = 2.7
amplitude_contrast = 0.07
# From the EMD-16721 header: nominal_defocus_min 1.5, nominal_defocus_max 4.5 um.
# Relaxed outward to [1, 5] um, which is what the notes prescribe for turning a
# paper's stated range into ctffind bounds. Constrains the wide first pass over
# the near-zero-tilt view; the second pass then searches a narrow window around
# whatever that found. Cs is NOT in the EMDB header for this entry - only the
# paper has it - but at this fit limit Cs contributes under 1% of the CTF phase,
# so the Krios objective value stands.
min_defocus_angstrom = 10000
max_defocus_angstrom = 50000

[reconstruct]
# NOT left unset, and not a preference. Derived thickness comes from Tiltalign's
# "thickness needed to contain centers of all fiducials", which measures specimen
# depth only when the fiducials sample it — gold beads on two faces do, patches
# do not. On TS_0002 it derived 25 bin8 px: a 24 nm box for a FIB lamella, and
# reconstruction reported `pass` on it. find_slab then found the specimen filling
# 84% of the box with 10% contrast, which is its own "not seeing the specimen"
# band: there was no vacuum in the volume to find an edge against.
#
# 320 is a generous first pass, the value TS_0005 used for a 177 px lamella. Snug
# it per series from find_slab once the reconstruction actually contains vacuum:
# lamella + ~25 px for residual X axis tilt across a 512 px field + edge margin.
thickness = 320

[template]
emdb_id = "EMD-16721"     # human 80S ribosome, untreated cells, same data
low_pass_angstrom = 19.6  # bin8 Nyquist
# Mask and box as pytom's own tutorial and usage notes have them (checked
# 2026-10-15): the radius a little past the particle, a soft edge ("a smooth
# fall-off to prevent aliasing artifacts"; --sigma "0.5-1.0 are usually
# sufficient for tomograms with 20A-10A voxel sizes"), and a box with "some
# overhang on purpose ... to ensure sufficient sampling in Fourier space of the
# weighting functions". The tutorial puts its ~300 A ribosome in 60 px at
# 13.79 A, 2.8x the diameter.
#
#   particle radius   290 / 2 / 9.784 = 14.8 px
#   mask radius       14.8 + 3        = 18 px, plus a 1 px gaussian edge
#   box               2 * 290 / 9.784 = 59.3 -> 60 px
#
# Until then the mask was 17 px with a hard edge, and the box 39 px: EMD-16721's
# own 380 A box, 1.3x the particle, taken by default. Not derived from the
# measured extent: that catches 32 px of a low-passed map's periphery, and with
# the 1.2 margin on top half the mask would be noise. The 3 px past the widest
# point is a colleague's rule; pytom's tutorial uses about 1 px plus the edge.
mask_radius_px = 18
mask_sigma_px = 1.0
box_size_px = 60

[pick]
# 290 A is the human 80S diameter that pytom's own documentation uses as its
# worked example. It sets the angular sampling through Crowther. The measured
# extent from prepare-template reads a few per cent under true (~274 A), so the
# literature value is the conservative choice here.
particle_diameter_angstrom = 290.0
# The best 600 peaks per tomogram with no score floor (cut_off = 0); the
# threshold is then read off the score curves in the report. 600 is about twice
# the ribosomes a biologist counted in the five MDC tomograms (288-362), the
# usual rule of thumb; the published work on this dataset took the best 800 and
# let classification find the real ones.
#
# This replaces a false-positive floor (number_of_false_positives = 100, cut-off
# from the noise model). On these tomograms the lane's score map did not see the
# specimen at all (2026-10-15: on TS_0005 44% of its top 100 peaks in the
# lamella, where noise puts 48%), so no floor could have made its picks real. A
# floor means something once the map does; until then a fixed count is the
# honest setting. The two are alternatives and run_series refuses both at once.
number_of_particles = 600
cut_off = 0.0
tophat_filter = false
gpu_ids = "0"

# Without these the match runs across the whole band, out to the bin8 Nyquist of
# 19.6 A, where a ribosome has little signal and the tomogram has plenty of
# noise. That flattens the score volume: the first run produced a cut-off of
# 0.1159 with the only two survivors at 0.1161 and 0.1184, which is a
# distribution with no peaks in it at all rather than a threshold set too high.
#
# 35 A was chosen first, to keep the ribosome's shape and drop detail that at
# this binning is mostly noise. Measured in real pytom on 2026-10-15
# (scripts/pick_ablation.sbatch, MDC jobs 3640899 and 3643100): the share of the
# 100 best peaks inside the lamella, with what noise would give in brackets, the
# best peak, and the peaks above the one-false-positive height.
#
#                                        TS_0463 (40%)        TS_0306 (75%)
#   39 px template, 35 A, RPC + CTF      89%   7.75   13      71%   7.48    4
#   60 px template, 25 A, RPC + CTF      87%   7.90   11      77%   7.83    6
#     the same without RPC               95%   8.33   41      73%   7.50    4
#     without RPC or CTF weighting       93%  12.30  241      99%  15.51   18
#     the same at 35 A                   94%  11.23  212     100%  14.31   17
#
# The first row is the lane as it was: on TS_0306 its map was blind, at the
# level noise gives. Dropping both corrections is what made either series' map
# see the lamella, and 25 A then beats 35 A by about a seventh more significant
# peaks at ~2.7x the orientations (pytom's Crowther step 4.9 against 6.9 deg).
# pytom's own tutorial matches at 1.3-1.45x Nyquist; 25 A is 1.28x here. The
# template and the low-pass changed together in row 2, so the 60 px box and
# soft mask are pytom's practice rather than a measured gain.
low_pass_angstrom = 25.0
# Off since 2026-10-15 (table above). It subtracts what a phase-randomised
# template of the same spectrum also matches, and on these tomograms that takes
# most of the ribosome's signal with it: alone it cost TS_0463 three quarters of
# its significant peaks. Worth trying again once reconstructions are sharper.
random_phase_correction = false
# Off since 2026-10-15 (table above). |CTF| weighting leans the match on the
# 35-60 A band, which these reconstructions barely carry: with it TS_0306's map
# stayed blind even without random-phase correction. A stand-in matcher showed
# {{USER}}'s etomo reconstruction of TS_0002 keeping its peaks under the same
# weighting, so this is about the reconstructions, not the weighting.
ctf_weighting = false
# Weights the CTF and the missing wedge per view rather than as one average, and
# is also what lets the accumulated dose in through --dose-accumulation: without
# it pytom has nothing to do with a dose file. The dose comes from the mdoc's
# PriorRecordDose, which is already accumulated in acquisition order — the order
# a dose-symmetric series was shot in, not the tilt order it is stored in.
per_tilt_weighting = true
# Flattens the tomogram's power spectrum before correlating. Standard practice
# for template matching in tomograms, and it was off.
spectral_whitening = true

[extract]
box_size_px = 48          # 470 A at 9.78 A/px, ~1.5x the particle

[executables]
# $PYTOMO_MP_DIR — note the O; $PYTOM_MP_DIR is unset and expands to nothing.
pytom_create_template = "$PYTOMO_MP_DIR/pytom_create_template.py"
pytom_create_mask = "$PYTOMO_MP_DIR/pytom_create_mask.py"
pytom_match_template = "$PYTOMO_MP_DIR/pytom_match_template.py"
pytom_extract_candidates = "$PYTOMO_MP_DIR/pytom_extract_candidates.py"
